3.speaker: Petr Vectern
3.text: "Good morning! Time to finally get this proposal going."

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Petr placed the draft in front of me.

5.speaker: Lucian Galade
5.text: "After your modifications, we will be starting the process, sir."

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Not long after, Petr and Lucian arrived.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: I was walking to my office, since today was the day to edit and make the final changes for the proposal to change the Constitution of Sordland.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: The reform committee finally bore tangible results and the draft of the changes were about to be presented.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: I walked in the marble corridors of the Palace, thinking about the massive steps we were about to take.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: My secretary Livia greeted me at the entrance to my office.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "Maybe we shouldn't mess with the Court much to keep them on our side."

16.speaker: Lucian Galade
16.text: "We could try to make the impeachment process more difficult or entirely get rid of it. A change like this would give you free reign. However, that might be going a little too far."

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: "We can start talking about Section 3. This is about the impeachment process of the President. Currently, in cases of high treason and breaking the Constitution, the Supreme Court may impeach and try the President."

18.speaker: Petr Vectern
18.text: "This law is particularly dangerous for you in this case. We will be going against the Old Guard, and if we prove to be successful in the Assembly..."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "We could add the Assembly in the process but make impeachment possible only with an absolute majority."

20.speaker: Petr Vectern
20.text: "...They will be looking for anything they can declare unconstitutional to tackle you. All they need is the Supreme Court to impeach you."

21.speaker: Petr Vectern
21.text: "We could try to balance it with the reformists and make it dependent on an enabling act from the Assembly. Sure, it would make the whole process longer but as long as we have a majority, nothing really changes."

22.speaker: Lucian Galade
22.text: "And the last one is the question about Soll's legacy. Basically his *Member of Honor* law. It gave him absolute immunity even when he's retired. He is a permanent member of the Assembly as well, but luckily he doesn't really attend anymore."

23.speaker: Lucian Galade
23.text: "We will leave it to the President to decide."

24.speaker: Lucian Galade
24.text: "That's a good idea. That'd make impeachment close to impossible."

26.speaker: Player
26.text: "No, I think we should respect this law."

27.speaker: Petr Vectern
27.text: "Hey, if people keep electing one person, that means they really are content. The masses are scared of change."

28.speaker: Lucian Galade
28.text: "This is regarding the appointment of ministers. Currently, the President is free to appoint anyone from the members of the Assembly. Nobody else is involved with the process."

30.speaker: Petr Vectern
30.text: "Yes, we'll need the help of some of the Judges in the process. Keeping some of their powers might make them more willing to get in dialogue with us."

31.speaker: Lucian Galade
31.text: "Now I'll move unto the 8th Section. We are reaching the end."

33.speaker: Lucian Galade
33.text: "It's the question about the immunity of the Judges. While the Anti-Old Guard sentiment is increasing, there are talks that taking away their immunity would give us authority over judiciary."

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."

36.speaker: Petr Vectern
36.text: "Unlikely to have 100% vote to pass. But I hear you."

37.speaker: Petr Vectern
37.text: "If we can remove their immunity or define an impeachment process, we could clean the Court from Orso and his gang."

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "Yes, they are already trying to hit you since they are expecting reforms. But we aim to cooperate with some of the judges to make sure that doesn't happen."

39.speaker: Player
39.text: "What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "We'll get rid of this law entirely."

42.speaker: Lucian Galade
42.text: "I agree, we could keep that in."

43.speaker: Lucian Galade
43.text: "So there is no reason to change this unless you want to sell this to the opposition parties. Sharing the power with the Assembly may make them sympathetic to you. This might be important for the NFP as well."

44.speaker: Petr Vectern
44.text: "Yes, but this is a delicate matter. The party, and I mean, not even Albin wants us to change the threshold. They think that... this would destroy our party in the long term."

45.speaker: Petr Vectern
45.text: "I'm sure some of the reformists may support that."

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."

48.speaker: Lucian Galade
48.text: "That is not bad idea. As long as we are the majority in the Assembly, that does not change too much."

49.speaker: Lucian Galade
49.text: "Some reformists suggested that the Assembly should nominate the ministers before the President approves them."

50.speaker: Petr Vectern
50.text: "Of course, according to the ratio of the party's in government. In our case, it's only us."

51.speaker: Lucian Galade
51.text: "Not wrong. The ten percent threshold is what that allowed us to control half of the Assembly with around one third of the majority in the elections."

52.speaker: Lucian Galade
52.text: "The fifth section is about our infamous electoral threshold. Most reformists want to lower the threshold as much as possible. We could try working with them but it is simpler to keep the law."

53.speaker: Lucian Galade
53.text: "Yes. Tarquin Soll governed for twenty years. It seems his magic is slowly vanishing from the minds of the people, for they believe term limits are necessary."

54.speaker: Petr Vectern
54.text: "Two major left parties; the Communist Party of Sordland and the Workers Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Lucian continued with the next section.

58.speaker: Player
58.text: "We should definitely work to decrease the threshold to some degree."

59.speaker: Player
59.text: "Do you think it would really hurt the party?"

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "A decrease is out of the question."

61.speaker: Player
61.text: "Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "It's not unfair that former Presidents get some special treatment."

64.speaker: Player
64.text: "After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."

66.speaker: Lucian Galade
66.text: "That is pretty powerful, indeed. That may scare some of our ministers too if you decide to *rule by decree.*"

67.speaker: Petr Vectern
67.text: "But it would be tougher to persuade the judges with this. Mrs. Edmonds and Mr. Garaci may not want to cooperate with you if they believe you're going to get rid of them afterwards."

68.speaker: Petr Vectern
68.text: "Sure. You'll have some time before we start writing the final proposal together."

69.speaker: Lucian Galade
69.text: "A decrease would definitely hurt our position in the future. If another party is elected to the Assembly, our projected vote would be closer to the real vote, which is significantly lesser."

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: "That's a possibility. It might make the reformists more willing to consider the changes."

71.speaker: Petr Vectern
71.text: "But if we keep the same voter base, say a 15% threshold, it would keep NFP out of the Assembly, leaving only two parties. Unless, Frens also falls back behind. But I doubt that."

72.speaker: Petr Vectern
72.text: "I agree. This really has no importance for the new Constitution. Also, Soll was a hero for many Sords, whether we like it or not."

73.speaker: Petr Vectern
73.text: "That would be enough to hold him accountable for his actions but why would you want to keep such the title then?"

75.speaker: Petr Vectern
75.text: "Oh, so you want to use the same privilege after all."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "Every President should gain that title after their term."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."

78.speaker: Lucian Galade
78.text: "10% seems already too high for many, sir. An increase may bring too much attention on the amendments."

80.speaker: Petr Vectern
80.text: "But don't forget that the Communist Party of Sordland and the Worker's Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "I will instead give the President the ability to replace Judges as necessary."

84.speaker: Lucian Galade
84.text: "We are at the 6th. This is about the presidential decrees. You already know that the reformists want them to be removed or limited. But I'm guessing you do not want any changes to your already powerful decrees, sir."

85.speaker: Lucian Galade
85.text: "For now I'll move onto the next one: Term Limits.

86.speaker: Petr Vectern
86.text: "Decreasing the threshold might mean opening their way into the Assembly."

87.speaker: Petr Vectern
87.text: "You would be opening their way into the parliament in the future if you were to decrease the threshold. It is important that you realize this."

88.speaker: Petr Vectern
88.text: "An increase on the other hand is more complex. NFP could be out of the Assembly but that would mean PFJP's seats would get higher too, if we're left with only two parties in the Assembly."

89.speaker: Petr Vectern
89.text: "I think some of the reformists really want to try him for his crimes during his terms. Especially against the Bludish. This law really has symbolic importance for both them and the Sollists."

90.speaker: Lucian Galade
90.text: "Me neither. I think it's important that the President can act quickly on matters of national importance."

91.speaker: Petr Vectern
91.text: "That's why only Tarquin Soll has it. He gave it to himself right after his military coup. This law is basically made to save the Colonel."

93.speaker: Lucian Galade
93.text: "Mr. Ricter will probably demand that we remove them completely. I doubt that this would be enough to get him to sit down with us."

94.speaker: Lucian Galade
94.text: "According to the Constitution, the Member of Honor not only has legal immunity but the state also covers most of their expenses as well as providing security at all times. It can only be given to someone by an absolute majority vote in the Assembly and the approval of the President."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet."

98.speaker: Petr Vectern
98.text: "That might be the best thing to do for now. If we agitate the Court further, we might lose our chances with Mrs. Edmonds as well."

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "We should strengthen the decrees further, so they have priority over statute law."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "We can't just give away our majority like that anyway."

102.speaker: Player
102.text: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly."

103.speaker: Player
103.text: "We should open their way and unite the left."

106.speaker: Petr Vectern
106.text: "Even Mr. Clavin and our party's reformist wing has no problems with the current law. USP would fully support that decision. I guess we could also persuade Mr. Kibener somehow."

107.speaker: Player
107.text: "I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "Yes, we can make it dependent on enabling acts."

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: Lucian couldn't hide the surprised look on his face.

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "We should keep using the threshold to our advantage."

117.speaker: Lucian Galade
117.text: "Well, we can't know these for sure. In the last elections, the Communist Party of Sordland and the Workers Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent. One of them may very well increase their votes in the next years."

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: "You'll have some time to think about your decision, sir."

119.speaker: Lucian Galade
119.text: "That's very bold, sir. But I like it."

120.speaker: Lucian Galade
120.text: "That is a fair concern. We'll need to sway some of their members to succeed after all."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “Can we go over each of the points that are in discussion for the draft?”

123.speaker: Lucian Galade
123.text: "Well, apart from the first two sections of decreasing the Supreme Court's authority and limiting the presidential vetoes... Other sections are up to debate."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “I thank you all for your input.”

125.speaker: Petr Vectern
125.text: "Well, regardless of what you decide, we will need to work together to push this agenda."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: Livia left to hang up my coat. I entered my office and sat down.

136.speaker: Livia Suno
136.text: "Mr. Rayne -- can you give me a hint about your reform plans? If you ask me, taking away the judges' immunity is long overdue, but it might anger a lot of people in these halls..."

140.speaker: Livia Suno
140.text: "I hope you'll keep me informed. I'll take your coat now."

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: She paused before taking my coat. It looked like she had something on her mind.

144.speaker: Narrator
144.text: She averted her eyes away from me and smiled.

145.speaker: Player
145.text: “I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “You'll find out along with the rest of Sordland, sweetheart."
